transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Wells (Redwood AE), Priya Mehta (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Arcadia Procurement), Nisha Patel (Arcadia Legal), Marco Ruiz (Arcadia Platform), Sofia Hernandez (Arcadia FinOps)

Summary: quick kickoff to align commercial paths, legal redline expectations, and a technical pilot to validate throughput/latency for their regulated workloads. Focus on MSA/DPA timing, egress/egress-fees, KMS/SSO, and whether Private deployment is necessary vs Dedicated.

Topics: MSA redline timeline; DPA & data residency questions; SLA thresholds and SLOs; rate-card scenarios and burst capacity; pilot scope and success criteria; security artifacts (SOC2, penetration tests, KMS integration).

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick goal for today — align on the contract roadmap and who owns next steps so procurement and legal have clarity.
[00:12] Liam: yeah thanks Jordan, we're evaluating vendors, and two big things for us are the MSA queue and the cost model — especially egress. so we want a clear path to procurement signoff.
[00:25] Jordan: totally. i'll sketch three commercial paths — hosted, dedicated reserved, and private — and how the MSA/DPA timing differs. priya will cover what we need technically for the pilot.
[00:36] Priya: hi all, uh, quick note — for the pilot i recommend dedicated capacity so we can guarantee p95 under load; hosted can be noisy during spikes, and private is heavier lift but gives you the most control.
[00:49] Marco: clarification — by "dedicated" do you mean reserved GPU pools in your cloud, or dedicated on-prem hardware? because for our compliance we might need the latter for certain datasets.
[01:03] Priya: good call. when i say dedicated here it's Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools in your cloud region with VPC peering. the private on-prem package is a separate option and would require an implementation window.
[01:16] Nisha: from legal's standpoint we'll need the DPA and the MSA redline outline — especially clauses about data residency, egress fees, and KMS control. also SOC2 and any FedRAMP posture notes.
[01:29] Anika: we'll attach the security pack; it includes SOC2 Type II summary and a pen-test overview. we can also provide a KMS integration doc for customer-managed keys.
[01:41] Sofia: egress fees are a showstopper for our FinOps model — can you map typical egress scenarios? like sustained embeddings pipelines vs occasional bulk exports.
[01:55] Jordan: yes, we will provide concrete egress scenarios. one thing to watch: caching (prefix/KV cache) and batching can dramatically reduce egress and per-token bill. i'll include examples.
[02:08] Liam: timeline question — procurement wants a redline and a rate-card by mid-April to hit our Q2 vendor panel. is that realistic?
[02:20] Jordan: realistic if we move fast. redlines from Nisha by Apr 15 and we'll return counter-proposal same week. rate-card scenarios — we can get a first pass by Apr 14.
[02:33] Nisha: on indemnity and liability we have some standard language; there may be a couple of exceptions. also curious about data retention and access logs for audit.
[02:46] Priya: we can surface audit logs and per-token lineage in the console; retention windows are configurable — we'll list defaults and options in the security pack.
[02:59] Marco: for the pilot, can we validate 100 concurrent sessions with 2k average sequence length? we need see p95 < 300ms for short prompts and reasonable throughput for embeddings.
[03:14] Priya: that'll be helpful — i'll design a pilot to emulate that traffic shape. note that sequence length affects kernel selection and batching. we'll test both short and long-tail sequences.
[03:28] Sofia: on pricing, can you show committed throughput discounts vs pay-as-you-go and what happens if we exceed commit?
[03:41] Jordan: yes, committed reserved capacity has a lower unit price and a burst bucket for short spikes; exceed charges are tiered. i'll include a clear example.
[03:53] Liam: any other vendor hoops? e.g., escrow, audit access, or legal hold?
[03:59] Nisha: we usually ask for audit access and a clause for cooperation on subpoenas or legal hold. also, encryption at rest and in transit must be spelled out.
[04:12] Anika: KMS integration supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) and we can note HSM options. for audit we provide log exports and CloudTrail-compatible hooks.
[04:25] Jordan: if private/on-prem is pursued, we can provide a deployment plan and an extended timeline; that usually adds 6–10 weeks of integration.
[04:38] Marco: okay that helps. for bandwith and egress — do you have a recommendation for routing policies? we might want failover to a cheaper region for non-sensitive traffic.
[04:52] Priya: routing policies can be set by traffic classification — sensitive routes pinned to specific model variants and regions; fallback to cheaper variants is supported, but the DPA needs to permit cross-border routing.
[05:07] Sofia: good point on cross-border — some datasets are EU-only. we'll flag those in the DPA.
[05:15] Jordan: on SLA, we provide SLOs per tier. dedicated customers get higher p99 targets and an SLA credit scheme. i'll outline the SLA table in the rate-card doc.
[05:27] Liam: acceptance criteria for pilot? we need pass/fail measures so procurement can sign off.
[05:34] Priya: pilot success criteria: p95 under test load, throughput within 15% of expected, and no data exfiltration issues. also functional correctness — model output must meet agreed eval prompts.
[05:50] Nisha: can you provide sample eval prompts and the quality monitoring plan? we usually tie rollout to a small eval set.
[05:57] Priya: yes, we'll include an eval harness and a quality-monitoring readout. there's an automated regression alert we can enable during pilot.
[06:07] Marco: network connectivity — we need VPC peering and private link, and a clear egress path for backups.
[06:18] Anika: documented in the onboarding checklist. we can share the diagram and required firewall rules.
[06:28] Jordan: ok to recap and close: Nisha will share MSA redlines by Apr 15; Jordan will send first-pass rate-card and SLA table by Apr 14; Priya will deliver pilot plan by Apr 18; Anika will send security pack and onboarding checklist by Apr 16.
[06:46] Liam: sounds good. any blockers from Redwood?
[06:49] Jordan: none from commercial side; just need Nisha's redlines. Priya: no technical blockers, just test data and accounts for pilot — Marco and team will supply.
[06:58] Marco: we'll provision a staging VPC and a sample dataset that's scrubbed.
[07:03] Jordan: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff and send the docs.
[07:09] Sofia: thanks all.

End of transcript.
